question: Do stocks beat the market after insider open-market purchases, and which kinds of purchase work best?
sample: SEC Form 4 open-market purchases (code P), 2006 onward, one signal per company per filing day; study sample needs a verified price, raw price >= $1 and 20-day dollar volume >= $100K.
benchmark: SPY (buy-and-hold, same entry and exit days); secondary: equal-weighted survivor index
entry: open of the first session after the filing date; variant C enters at that session's close
significance: calendar-time portfolios held 63 sessions, monthly excess over SPY, Newey-West t (3 lags), Holm correction within each family
minimum_data: 200+ signals and 60+ usable months in discovery

strategies.proven_insider: Insiders whose earlier buys beat SPY
strategies.first_buy_exec: Exec's first buy in a year, $50K+

walk_forward: score threshold in {40, 50, 60, 70}, chosen each year from 2011 by calendar-time Sharpe on months already realized

verdict_rule.works: positive with Holm p < 0.05 in discovery AND same sign with Holm p < 0.05 in holdout AND positive under entry variant C AND positive against the survivor index AND positive in 60%+ of years
verdict_rule.not enough data: fails the minimum-data rule (decided on counts only)
